newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shortcovering lifts Singapore rubber, ends up.
newsitem.headline: Shortcovering lifts Singapore rubber, ends up.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly higher on Wednesday as shortcovering for nearby months by local players lifted the market with the trade expecting the mild buying to continue in the coming days, dealers said.
"We saw some speculative shortcovering by players trying to cover their positions. Most of the buying was concentrated in the nearby months," a trader in foreign brokerage house said.
Rubber dealers said the recent bout of shortcovering may continue until the end of the week.
"The pattern of fresh buying in the afternoon sessions will probably be repeated tomorrow," a trader said.
Most of the buying was for RSS3 rubber with the total traded reaching about 5,600 tonnes.
The volume of buying for RSS1 and TSR20 rubber reached about 1,100 tonnes each, dealers said.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 122.00-124.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 121.75 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 172.50-174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.23) a kg from the previous 172.50 cents.
April TSR20 was seen at 169.00-171.00 Singapore cents (US$1.19-$1.20) a kg from yesterday's 168.50 cents.
